svg.data-power-max-scope: HIG Connecting Power - measured at 40 C ambient, optics fully populated and 100% traffic load; 2545 W is the AC figure and 2279 W the DC one
svg.data-optics-osfp: 800GE OSFP OpenZR+/ZR/2xLR4/2xFR4/DR8+/DR8/SR8 and 400GE OSFP OpenZR+/ZR/ER4/LR4/FR4/SR8/DR4/DR4+/PLR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list); the HIG port table gives ports 0~63 as 400G/800G up to 2 km
svg.data-optics-sfp28: 1G/10G/25G on the management pair, up to 40 km per the HIG Port Overview table; the datasheet calls the same pair '2 x 10/25G SFP28 ports' and no module list is published for it
svg.data-optic-power-classes: sixteen ports take a 30 W optic and the other forty-eight take 16 W (HIG Figure 9). The 30 W ports are 0, 6, 8, 14, 16, 22, 24, 30, 33, 39, 41, 47, 49, 55, 57 and 63 - the first and fourth cage rows of columns 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 13 and 16 counting from the left
svg.data-timing: 1PPS and 10MHz SMB input/output (premium), 50 ohm, cable not to exceed 3 m; Stratum 3E OCXO holdover and ITU-T Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE). The datasheet's compatible cable row names 'SMB coaxial cable with 10-32UNF-2A connector for 1PPS and 10MHz', and the HIG offers a converter where the far end is BNC
svg.data-console: RJ45 RS-232 and micro-USB, both labelled IOIO, 115200 8N1 no flow control; the micro-USB needs a Silicon Labs CP210x driver (HIG Initial System Setup)
svg.data-oob: 1x RJ45 100/1000M plus the 2x SFP28 management pair
svg.data-emc: FCC Part 15, Subpart B, Class A; ICES-003, Class A; EN 55032, Class A; EN 300 386; EN 55035; VCCI CISPR 32, Class A
svg.data-nebs: NOT A CERTIFICATION - the HIG carries 'Cautions and regulatory compliance statements for NEBS': suitable for installation as part of the Common Bonding Network (CBN); an external Surge Protection Device must be used with AC powered equipment, installed at the AC power service entrance; can be installed in Network Telecommunications Facilities where the National Electric Code applies; the DC input terminals are DC-I (isolated DC return) and the RTN terminal should be isolated from the chassis or rack; the intra-building OOB Ethernet port is suitable for connection to intra-building or unexposed wiring only (Type 2, 4 or 4a per GR-1089). No NEBS level is claimed anywhere in the held documents
svg.data-installation: restricted-access server or computer room only; suitable for Information Technology Rooms per Article 645 of the National Electrical Code and NFPA 75

The OSFP faceplate is what separates this from the S9321-64E, which is the same chassis with 64 QSFP-DD","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"spec/schemas/standards.yaml carries no `osfp` key, so std/osfp@1 - built for this device - declares `interface: osfp` instead of `conforms:`, and L9 therefore never checks its 23.10 x 13.50 mm aperture against anything. The number is measured off HIG Figure 8 and corroborated by the OSFP MSA module envelope (22.58 x 13.0 mm), which is not the same thing as the MSA's own faceplate-opening figure. The cage DEPTH, 47 mm, is a straight estimate: no held document dimensions an OSFP receptacle. The same absence shows up a second time in the tooling: lint's own PLUGGABLE_CAGES set lists eleven cage media and not osfp, so L40 skips the osfp-800g group and then reports `attrs.optics-osfp` as naming no group's media. THAT WARNING IS LEFT STANDING because it is true and it is this gap's own record - the optics list is correct and nothing in the toolchain can currently reach it through the media name.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["osfp-800g"],"wanted":"the OSFP MSA faceplate cutout and receptacle-depth figures, so the key can be added to the registry and std/osfp@1 can carry `conforms:`; and `osfp` added to lint's PLUGGABLE_CAGES so L40 can resolve the optics prose","what":"osfp-registry"},{"note":"The HIG's section 10 tables the six system lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the RJ45 management jack, and says nothing about the port lamps: not what the single lamp beside each OSFP means, and nothing at all about the SFP28 pair. Every port lamp keeps the off/on component default rather than an invented vocabulary.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["osfp-800g","sfp28-mgmt","port-leds"],"wanted":"a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states","what":"port-led-semantics"},{"note":"The two SFP28 cages are drawn belly-to-belly, the lower one rotate: 180, by analogy with the RJ45 pair four rows below it whose mirror IS resolvable in the front render. The SFP block itself is 15.7 mm wide in a 1.15 px/mm render and the guide draws modules seated in it, so neither image resolves the latch direction. If the pair is NOT mirrored the lower cage is drawn upside down.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["sfp28-mgmt"],"wanted":"a square-on close-up of the SFP28 block, or the unit in hand","what":"sfp-cage-orientation"},{"note":"sources-disagree on the fan, and the disagreement is recorded rather than reconciled away: the HIG Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 81.0 mm wide, while the rear render puts the bays on a measured 84.0 mm pitch (two independent feature families agreeing to 0.3 mm). The manifest carries the tabled 81.0 face on the measured 84.0 pitch, which reads as a 3 mm chassis web - the same resolution the S9300-32D family's fan needed, and an inference either way. HIG Figure 7, which would settle it, fails the aspect gate at 10.6% out and cannot be measured.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["rear","fans","psus"],"wanted":"an orthographic rear elevation or a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-808012, or a caliper across two adjacent fan bays","what":"rear-strip-width"},{"note":"The only images of the PSU and fan faces in place are HIG Figure 7 at roughly 2.9 px/mm and a 520 px product render. The FRU components those bays seat were built from the same material for the sibling S9321-64E; their outlines are the vendor's tabled dimensions but their face artwork - vent fields, handle, latch and lamp positions - is proportioned, not measured.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["ufispace/psu-302-ac@1","ufispace/psu-302-dc@1","ufispace/fan-808012@1"],"wanted":"square-on photographs of a PSU-302 and a FAN-808012 out of the chassis","what":"fru-face-detail"},{"note":"No held document prints an orderable chassis part number. The datasheet's configuration row says only 'Contact our sales team for current configuration options' and the HIG names the product as S9321-64E/EO throughout. Per the S9510-28DC precedent, orderable SKUs exist at the owner even when no PDF prints one, so the configurations carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["base","ac","dc"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs","what":"chassis-sku"},{"note":"The five rail attachment pins per side are described in words by the HIG and drawn without dimensions, so they are placed evenly and marked estimated, as is the compliance label on the underside. The six top-cover recesses come from a footprint drawing that is 8.4% stretched in its depth axis, so their y positions and heights are estimates on an even fit rather than measurements.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["left","right","bottom","top"],"wanted":"a UfiSpace mechanical drawing, or square-on photographs of the sides and underside","what":"side-and-underside-detail"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"3+1","redundancy-note":"3+1 - 3+1 hot-swappable (attrs fan-redundancy)"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster at the left edge - the RS-232 console RJ45, the micro-USB console that reaches the same UART, the USB 3.0 maintenance port, the out-of-band RJ45 and the recessed reset button","role":"management","term":"Port"},"osfp-800g":{"attrs":{"media":"osfp","speed":"800g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"port-leds":{"description":"one lamp per OSFP port, in the band above the upper bank and below the lower one","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 active-active hot-swappable"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"sfp28-mgmt":{"attrs":{"media":"sfp28","speed":"25g"},"description":"the stacked SFP28 pair the vendor numbers 64 and 65 - a second out-of-band path, 1G/10G/25G and up to 40 km per the HIG Port Overview table","index-origin":0,"role":"management","term":"Port"},"status-leds":{"description":"the chassis indicators - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and the blue ID beacon","index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"timing":{"description":"the two SMB timing interfaces, 1PPS and 10MHz, both input/output and 50 ohm; they discipline the Stratum 3E OCXO that SyncE runs from","index-origin":1,"role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"UfiSpace","maturity":"modelled","model":"S9321-64EO","name":"s9321-64eo","portfolio":{"also-listed-in":["Cloud & Data Centers"],"family":"Datacenter Switch for AI/ML","line":"AI Networking"},"provenance":{"attrs":"datasheet - Specifications, Performance, Environmental and Regulatory Compliance sections, transcribed into sections; timing from the datasheet's Timing and Timing Support rows and the HIG's 1PPS and 10MHz cabling sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied. THE NEBS STATEMENTS ARE THE HIG'S OWN WORDS and are a set of installation conditions, not a certification claim: the guide heads them 'Cautions and regulatory compliance statements for NEBS' and never says the product is certified to any NEBS level, so the attr says exactly that and no more.","cage-part":"drawing/registry - the ports are OSFP, not QSFP-DD: the HIG states it twice, in the Port Overview note ('The S9321-64E features 64x800G QSFP-DD ports, while the S9321-64EO is equipped with 64x800G OSFP ports') and in Figure 4's callout '64x 800G OSFP'. spec/schemas/standards.yaml HAS NO OSFP KEY and the library had no OSFP part, so std/osfp@1 was built for this device: 23.10 x 13.50 mm measured off Figure 8, which brackets the OSFP MSA module envelope of 22.58 x 13.0 mm. It declares `interface: osfp` rather than `conforms:`, which is the honest form while the registry entry does not exist. See the osfp-registry gap.","chassis":"datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 2RU, 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm', weight 23.74 kg without FRU for the EO specifically (the HIG's Component Physical Information table lists the two variants separately: S9321-64E 23.72 kg, S9321-64EO 23.74 kg, and this model carries the EO figure). 436 is the body between the ear planes, not a rack face - the HIG Space Clearance section says the 'chassis width is 17.16 inches (43.6cm) and is shipped with an adjustable mounting rail kit suited for standard 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', so the rack hardware is additional to 436 and is not drawn. Depth 762 is the chassis without FRUs; the same section adds 29 mm for the fan handle and 30 mm for the PSU handle beyond it.","figure-gating":"HIG Figure 8 carries an elevation of each variant. The EO one spans 1365 x 273 px across the 436 x 87.7 mm face - aspect 5.000 against a true 4.971, 0.57% out - so it is orthographic enough to carry geometry, and it is the ruler for the whole front at 3.131 px/mm. The front RENDER was gated too and passes better (501 x 101 px, aspect 4.960, 0.22% out) but resolves only 1.15 px/mm, so it is used for colour, counts, connector orientation and one plausibility check, not for positions. HIG Figure 7's rear elevation FAILS the gate - 1195 x 269 px is aspect 4.44 against 4.971, 10.6% out, because the drawing carries a perspective bevel along its top edge - so nothing on the rear is scaled off it; see the rear-layout note.","frus":"ufispace/psu-302-ac@1, ufispace/psu-302-dc@1 and ufispace/fan-808012@1 are REUSED, not built here: they were created for the sibling S9321-64E from the same shared S9321-64E/EO installation guide, and their 68 x 40.6 and 81 x 81.5 faces are the same numbers this model measured out of that guide's tables independently. Saying so matters - two files agreeing is evidence only when they were derived separately, and here the SOURCE is common even though the readings were not.","jack-orientation":"photo - at 26x on the front render the upper RJ45 shows its latch keyway UP with the eight contacts below, and the lower one shows the contacts UP with the keyway below, so the pair mirrors and the upper is drawn rotate: 180. WHICH IS WHICH WAS SETTLED BY THE LAMPS, not by the callout order: the lower jack carries a green lamp at its bottom-left and an amber one at its bottom-right, which is the HIG's Management port LED table (left green 1G, right amber 10M/100M), so the lower jack is the OOB port and the upper is the console. The panel legend agrees once read that way - 'IOIOI' with an up triangle for the console and a down triangle beside the network symbol for the OOB. common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 draws its two integrated lamps on the keyway side already, matching this device's photo; the mismatch common/rj45-hd@1 used to force (lamps drawn on the CONTACT side) is gone, and the jack stays unrotated because the contacts and keyway are geometry, unaffected by the lamp side.","lifecycle":"searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9321-64EO end of life' - no announcement found; the UfiSpace product page and distributor listings are live. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.","mgmt-block":"drawing/photo - the EO's left cluster is arranged DIFFERENTLY from the E's and was read off the EO elevation, not borrowed. Top to bottom: the 1PPS SMB jack centred (14.85, 9.80) and the 10MHz SMB centred (14.87, 24.04), both 7.4 mm across, in a honeycomb vent field, with a plain 5.9 mm round hole punched through that field at (6.6, 32.7) which no callout in Figure 4 names and which is drawn as decor rather than guessed at; the reset pinhole under a RESET legend; the model name; the micro-USB console; then a white six-row legend block at x 2.28-6.75, y 59.8-74.6 with its lamp column beside it at x 7.7-10.9 - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1 and a blue ID, which is HIG Figure 28's EO panel exactly (the E puts its lamps on the LEFT of the legend and its ID lamp separately above). The vertical USB 3.0 sits right of the lamps and the two RJ45s are stacked in a silver bezel at x 22.5-38.4, y 51.5-75.6, openings measured 53.78-61.49 and 65.67-73.38.","optic-power-map":"drawing - HIG Figure 9 marks sixteen ports in red on the EO panel and says '16 ports marked in red support 30W, while the remaining 48 ports support 16W'. The red blocks were measured against the column fit rather than counted by eye: they fall at 44.9-68.4, 116.0-163.7, 211.3-259.6, 306.5-355.5 and 402.5-425.9 mm in the FIRST and the FOURTH cage row and nowhere else, which is columns 0, 3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 12 and 15 - eight columns, two rows, sixteen ports, matching the vendor's own count. That resolves to ports 0, 6, 8, 14, 16, 22, 24, 30, 33, 39, 41, 47, 49, 55, 57 and 63. This is a fact about the ports that no structure in the schema can hold, so it is carried as an attr string as well as here.","part-numbers":"The FRU part numbers (PSU-302-AESR, PSU-302-DESR, FAN-808012-HCE) are datasheet ordering lines and live on the configurations and the FRU contracts. Only ONE fan type and ONE airflow direction are offered - the HIG says 'The S9321-64E/EO airflow direction is front-to-back' with no alternative, and the datasheet lists a single fan ordering line - so unlike the 1RU boxes in this library there is no blue/red airflow pair to model. NO ORDERABLE CHASSIS SKU appears in any held document; the datasheet says only 'Contact our sales team for current configuration options'.","port-grid":"drawing - HIG Figure 8, EO elevation at 3.131 px/mm. THE PORTS ARE IN FOUR ROWS OF SIXTEEN, not two rows of thirty-two: sixteen cage columns, each carrying two OSFP in the upper bank and two in the lower. Column geometry came from the thirty-two green port lamps above the upper bank, which resolve as sixteen evenly spaced PAIRS - column 0 centre 56.20 mm, column pitch 23.10 mm inside a group of four, group pitch 95.70 mm, fitted across all sixteen with a maximum residual of 0.25 mm. The sixteen drawn cage faces agree (first 44.7-67.1, last 400.9-424.5 against 44.65 and 424.15 predicted). Rows: the four cage bands measure 12.21-25.70, 27.31-41.12, 48.51-62.00 and 63.93-77.42 mm, read off the bright bezel divider between each pair, so the parts are laid at 12.20, 27.55, 48.50 and 63.85, and each band is 13.5 mm tall - which is the OSFP module's own 13.0 mm height plus a cage bezel, a second reason to believe the reading. THE ROWS WERE MEASURED TWICE. The front render's black cage openings put the four row centres at 18.24, 32.99, 55.14 and 69.90 against the figure's 18.96, 34.22, 55.26 and 70.68 - agreement to 0.12 mm on the third row and 1.23 mm at worst on the second. The figure's numbers are the ones carried: it resolves 3.131 px/mm against the render's 1.149, where one render pixel is already 0.87 mm, and what the render shows is the dark hole inside the cage rather than the aperture the figure draws. The residual is recorded rather than split, because splitting two readings is a third number neither source states. Numbering from the elevation's own blue numerals and the HIG Port Overview table ('Port ID 0~63 QSFP-DD or OSFP'): each column carries an even port above the odd one below it, left to right, 0..31 in the upper bank and 32..63 in the lower.","port-leds":"drawing - two round lamps per column in the band above each bank, the left lamp belonging to the even (upper) port and the right one to the odd (lower) port, at the column centre -/+ 1.90 mm. Lamp rows measured at y 9.93-12.50 above the upper bank (centre 11.2) and 80.57-82.50 below the lower one (centre 81.6). The blue port numeral sits outboard of each lamp with a white triangle between them - the triangle points up for the even port and down for the odd, which is how the vendor disambiguates the pair. THE TRIANGLES ARE NOT MODELLED: sixty-four more silkscreen marks whose whole content is already carried by the numerals they sit under. Recorded here rather than left silent.","power":"datasheet 'Typical power: 925 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. The HIG gives TWO maxima, one per input type - 'The maximum system power consumption is 2279 watts' in the DC procedure and '2545 watts' in the AC one - and unusually it QUALIFIES them: 'Testing criteria for maximum power are as follows: Temperature 40 C, Optics: full populated, Traffic: 100% load'. That is a fully-configured measurement, and it is a different scope from the bare typical figure, so the two are carried as two facts and not reconciled. power-max-w takes the AC figure, 2545, because max means the highest; the DC figure is recorded beside it. PSU rating 3000 W per supply; at a 110 V AC input each supply delivers only 1500 W and hot-swap redundancy is lost (HIG note).","rear-layout":"measured on the REAR RENDER, not on HIG Figure 7. That figure is a three-quarter view with a perspective bevel along its top edge and is 10.6% wrong in aspect, so it gives only what is on the face and in what order; the render (-3-view) spans 508 x 101 px across the 436 x 87.7 mm face, aspect 5.03 against a true 4.971 and 1.2% out, so it carries geometry at 1.165 px/mm. THE FAN BAY PITCH IS 84.0 mm AND NOT THE 81.0 mm THE HIG TABLES: two independent feature families on that render agree on it - the red airflow tags at x 11.2, 95.3, 179.4 and 265.2 and the fan status lamps at 18.5, 102.6, 186.3 and 270.0, whose successive gaps run 83.7 to 85.8 and average 84.0 - and the fourth grille ends at 337, which 4 x 84 from x 4.0 reproduces exactly. The 81.0 mm the HIG's Component Physical Information table gives the fan module is drawn as the module FACE, leaving a 3 mm chassis web between bays, which is the same body-versus-face split the S9300-32D family shows and which the render's thin dark seams support. The PSU faces are the tabled 68 x 40.6 - Figure 5 prints those two numbers on the drawing - and sit at x 358.0 with their top edges at y 3.0 and 45.0, read off the render's PSU lamps at x 359.5 and its release tabs at 426.6-430.9. Between fan 3 and PSU0 the 21 mm strip carries the silver grounding plate with two M4 lug holes at (350, 10) and (350, 25), the earth symbol and the FAN 0 1 2 3 legend, which is where the render puts them and where the HIG's grounding section says the lug goes ('located on the rear of the router').","sfp-block":"drawing - one stacked SFP28 pair in a silver ganged frame at x 24.15-39.80, y 12.50-44.62, the vendor's ports 64 and 65 printed in orange inside it. The two drawn module faces sit at y 17.67-25.70 and 32.77-41.12, so the 10 mm std/sfp apertures are centred on 21.69 and 36.95. The datasheet calls them '2 x 10/25G SFP28 ports' and the HIG Port Overview table gives ports 64~65 as SFP28, 1G/10G/25G, up to 40 km, while Figure 4's callout calls the same pair '2x 10G SFP+ Management'; the table's wider range is what the group carries. The lower cage is drawn rotate: 180 on the same belly-to-belly reasoning as the RJ45 pair, but the latch direction is NOT resolvable in any held image at this block's size - see the sfp-cage-orientation gap. THE 64 AND 65 NUMERALS ARE MOVED OFF THE CAGES: Figure 8 prints them on the drawn module faces, where a seated transceiver would cover them, so they are placed in the frame bands immediately above each cage - the only spans of that frame a module does not fill. Their exact printed position is not resolvable in the 1.15 px/mm render.","sources":"UfiSpace S9321-64EO datasheet (working/intake/ufispace/converted/s9321-64eo-datasheet) for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, timing, power, environment and compliance; S9321-64E/EO Hardware Installation Guide (s9321-64eo-hig) - one document covering both variants - for the system overview, the EO's own front elevation, the port and optic-power tables, the FRU dimension drawings, the LED tables, grounding and rack mounting; three vendor renders (photos/s9321-64eo-1-view isometric, -2-view front, -3-view rear) for colour, orientation and construction. WHERE THE GUIDE DRAWS BOTH VARIANTS THE EO ELEVATION WAS USED, never the E: the two differ in cage type and in how the left cluster is arranged, and Figure 4 gives them different callout lists.","vent-islands":"derived - a vent field is a perforation and the drawing said so, but the marks printed inside one were floating on air (L64). The vendor interrupts the perforation where it prints, so each of those marks now has a solid patch under it in the chassis colour, drawn over the vent the way ufispace/s9600-72xc paints its port bands over one. The patch is the printing's own footprint plus 0.4 mm, which is what the S9610-36D's front render measures: its slots stop 0.4 mm outside each lamp cluster and resume 0.4 mm past it. Where a vent is simply measured wider than the metal it reaches, this states the metal that the printing proves is there without re-measuring the field.","views":"Six views. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and HIG Figure 4, whose footprint drawing prints the fan handles at the top; six long stadium recesses run across the cover on a measured 90 mm pitch from 161 mm, and their depth positions are ESTIMATED because that drawing is 8.4% stretched in its depth axis (it draws 436 x 762 at aspect 0.524 against a true 0.572) - the x extents are fractions of a width the same drawing gets right. BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries the compliance sticker at an estimated position. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): each carries the five rail attachment pins the HIG rack-mounting section describes ('The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins'), evenly spaced and ESTIMATED - no held drawing dimensions them.
